Title: Five men arrested in connection with assault with weapons in Petaling Jaya
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Police arrested five men, aged between 30 and 40, on suspicion of being involved in an attack on a man using dangerous weapons at a housing area here yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said police seized a parang and a saw believed to have been used in the incident.
"At 1:03am yesterday, the district police headquarters received a police report from a local man stating that he had been attacked by several people. Police also tracked down a video related to the incident that went viral on social media," he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin added that three of those arrested had criminal records.
"The case is investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for possessing weapons or dangerous objects during a riot. The public is advised not to spread inaccurate information or make any speculations regarding this incident," he said.
Shamsudin urged witnesses to come forward to the nearest police station or contact the district headquarters operations room directly at 03-79662222.

Title: Two women killed in five-vehicle crash in Setiu
Article:
SETIU: Two women were killed when the Proton Waja car they were travelling in was involved in a five-vehicle collision at Km48 Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Baru in Kampung Selamat here this afternoon.
The victims were identified as the driver, trader Nur Fauziah Ismail, 38, from Kampung Apek, and front-seat passenger Zawiah Halias, 41, a trader from Kampung Hulu Kekabu.
District police chief Superintendent Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the crash about 4pm.
The incident, he said, is believed to have occurred about 3.45pm.
He said initial investigations showed that the Proton Waja travelling from Kota Baru towards Kuala Terengganu was believed to have skidded into the opposite lane before colliding with a trailer lorry.
"Following the collision, the trailer also skidded and grazed a Perodua Aruz multi-purpose vehicle, a Perodua Myvi and a UDT lorry travelling from Kota Baru towards Kuala Terengganu," he said in a statement.
He said both victims were pronounced dead at the scene and their bodies sent to the Setiu Hospital forensics unit.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Zahril said witnesses should contact the district police headquarters Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department to assist investigations.

Title: Anthropic AI model sent fake murder tip to Philadelphia police
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia police, authorities said Friday, criticising the company for taking two months to report the incident.
The Philadelphia Police Department said the false submission was made in July through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a public website where people can share information about unsolved killings.
According to Anthropic's account, as relayed by police, the model was running a test that involved interacting with randomly selected websites when it reached the site and filed false information about an unsolved murder.
The AI model presented itself as someone who might have knowledge of the case.
The incident echoed other recent cases of unintended behavior involving AI models, including one where an OpenAI agent undergoing a security evaluation broke out of its testing environment and breached systems at AI platform Hugging Face.
Anthropic's breaches have prompted the White House to mandate that AI companies notify and correct security incidents, news outlet Axios reported citing administration officials.
"This notification and remediation process is not optional... It is a critical national security obligation," White House Super Intelligence Force leaders said in a statement to Axios.
The episode heightened concerns about the industry's increased use of AI agents, systems programmed to take multi-step actions without human supervision.
Anthropic published a report Friday outlining multiple types of "unintended" actions that its models have taken, including the incident involving the Philadelphia Police Department website.
Other organisations impacted included the White House and other US government agencies, the report said.
The newly revealed incidents "had minimal real-world impact" and were "significantly less severe" than other cybersecurity incidents previously reported, Anthropic said.
'UNACCEPTABLE' DELAY
The company outlined four categories of incidents that it found during an internal review of its Claude model: exploiting "basic" coding flaws, submitting forms on websites, bypassing requirements for tokens or fees, and using short URLs to get around other limits.
Anthropic has turned off internet access for Claude during all internal testing for now "until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures... reliably catch behaviors like these," the report said.
Philadelphia police said the phony tip, dated July 18, was flagged as spam and never reached the department's Real-Time Crime Centre for vetting.
They added that there was no sign that police systems had been breached or department data compromised.
Anthropic discovered the incident on September 28, shut down the automated testing process responsible and added a new validation step for future tests, police said.
The company alerted the department on October 7, and the two sides met the following day.
"The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable," the department said.
Police said their safeguards had limited the impact, but that these "do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide."
"Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers," the statement added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor extends closure of all schools, religious institutions until Oct 16
Article:
JOHOR BARU: All schools and educational institutions in Johor, including religious schools, will remain closed for another five days from Monday until Oct 16 due to worsening haze and unhealthy air quality.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made after considering prevailing air pollution conditions and in deference to the decree of Regent of Johor Tunku Ismail, who prioritises the safety, health and well-being of Johoreans, particularly students and education personnel.
He said air pollutant index (API) readings remained between 170 and 180, with no significant improvement, indicating that air quality continued to be unhealthy.
"The expected wind movement from Kalimantan between Oct 13 and 15 could bring transboundary air pollution, affecting air quality in Johor.
"The risk of rising concentrations of fine particles in the atmosphere, which could affect the respiratory system and the health of students and vulnerable groups, was also taken into account," he said in a statement today.
Naqib said stagnant atmospheric conditions and limited air movement could further hinder the dispersion of pollutants, potentially prolonging the haze.
He added that reports on the health effects of air pollution, particularly respiratory problems among children and school communities, were also considered before the decision was made.
Meanwhile, state Islamic Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the extended closure also covered Johor Religious Schools, Johor Government Religious Secondary Schools and registered private Islamic education institutions under the Johor Islamic Religious Department (JAINJ).
He said the decision followed the state government's announcement extending the closure of educational institutions throughout Johor.
Home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) will continue during the closure, subject to the directives of the Johor State Education Department and JAINJ, respectively.
Any assessments or academic examinations affected by the closure will be rescheduled according to the arrangements set by the relevant authorities.
Both Naqib and Fared urged parents and guardians to monitor their children's health, limit outdoor activities and ensure they drink sufficient water.
They also advised parents to seek prompt medical attention if their children experience persistent coughing, sore throats, breathing difficulties or other symptoms associated with air pollution.
The state government, in collaboration with the relevant agencies, will continue monitoring API readings.
Any decision on when schools and religious institutions can resume normal operations will be announced through official channels, subject to improvements in air quality and assessments of health and safety conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu open tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual tomorrow as Air Pollutant Index readings in the three states remain under control.
The states observe a Friday-Saturday weekend, making Sunday a school day.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the decision was based on the latest air quality readings.
"The Education Ministry will continue to monitor developments in air quality from time to time," she said in a statement today.
Data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed all monitoring stations in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu recorded readings below 100 as of 8pm today.
Kemaman recorded the highest reading in Terengganu at 89, while Sungai Petani recorded 80 in Kedah and Kota Bharu recorded 76 in Kelantan.
All readings fall within the moderate range of 51 to 100, below the unhealthy threshold of 101.
On Oct 8, Fadhlina
announced the closure
of all schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as schools in Rompin, Pahang, following the worsening haze.
The Education Ministry has stipulated that all educational institutions under its purview in areas recording
API readings above 180
must close from Oct 9.
Institutions in areas recording API readings above 150 for three consecutive days must also close from Oct 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Abbas postpones Palestinian legislative elections to September next year
Article:
RAMALLAH, Palestinian Territories: Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections to September next year, official media said, confirming widespread speculation over the polls which were last held in 2006.
The vote will be held alongside presidential elections on Sept 11, 2027, Abbas said in a decree, blaming "obstacles" imposed by Israel, according to the Palestinian Wafa news agency.
The legislative elections, which the international community has strongly advocated for, had been scheduled for Nov 28 this year, while a presidential vote was expected in early 2027.
Israel had blasted Abbas's Palestinian Authority as "corrupt" over the anticipated delay.
"Abbas issued a presidential decree on Saturday calling for simultaneous presidential and legislative elections to be held on Sept 11, 2027," Abbas's office said in a statement published by Wafa.
The presidency blamed the delay on "obstacles imposed by Israeli measures that prevent elections from being held on their previously scheduled date, as well as the need to create appropriate political, security and on-the-ground conditions to ensure free, fair and inclusive elections."
This week, Abbas' Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority said Israel refused to allow Palestinian election officials access to east Jerusalem or Gaza ahead of the legislative elections.
Israel's foreign minister Gideon Saar on Friday had accused Abbas of "fooling the international community" by planning to postpone upcoming legislative polls.
Holding polls is part of the reforms demanded by the international community for the Palestinian Authority, including the European Union.
The last legislative elections in the Palestinian territories were held in 2006, when Islamist movement Hamas won. They defeated Fatah, which dominates the Palestinian Authority.
The ensuing rift set off a round of factional fighting, with Hamas later seizing power in the Gaza Strip and creating a territorial divide between Fatah in the West Bank and Hamas in Gaza.
As a result, the Palestinian Legislative Council, which is the PA's parliament, has not met since 2007.
Abbas won the last Palestinian presidential election in 2005, and his term should have expired in 2009, but he has since ruled by decree.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johari Ghani: Focus of 2027 Budget was to lighten the people's burdens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget was an effort by the government to ease the public's burdens through financial assistance, individual tax relief and tax reductions for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the approach included several measures to help the public cope with daily living expenses while easing the financial burden on workers and businesses.
Speaking after officiating the closing ceremony of the Johari Ghani Cup National Sports Day Futsal Carnival in Batu Caves, he said the measures also included financial assistance to help the public afford essential goods, with the amount of aid varying according to the recipient category.
"I noticed that in the budget announcement, the prime minister placed considerable emphasis on reducing the cost of living. There are various ways to address the cost of living.
"First, increasing financial assistance to help people purchase goods, supplementing their income with aid provided by the government.
"Second, providing some relief to salaried workers who have to pay taxes by allowing deductions and reducing their tax burden. Although the reductions may not be substantial, everyone can feel the benefits overall," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Don't reshare provocative 3R content, report it to authorities
Article:
MELAKA: The public have been advised against sharing social media content that insults, provokes or incites hostility over religion, race and the royal institution (3R), and instead to report such content to the authorities for further action.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said resharing such content would only widen its reach, including by increasing its view count on social media.
"Do not help spread it, do not reshare it, do not give it views. File a police report or lodge a complaint with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
"Both responsible agencies will take immediate action," he told reporters after officiating at the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) 2026 with the Paya Rumput@Tangga Batu community at the Krubong People's Housing Project (PPR) here today.
Fahmi was responding to a social media post by influencer Lim Sian See, whose real name is Datuk Eric Se-To, questioning the use of the word "lighad" in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's speech when tabling the Supply Bill (Budget 2027) in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
In the post, Lim questioned the word before making a sarcastic association with another word.
The word "lighad", which appears in verse 18 of Surah al-Hasyr, refers to tomorrow or the future.
Fahmi said police and MCMC were tracing the individual to assist in investigations and have a statement recorded, adding that any further action would depend on the findings and the prosecution's consideration.
"We have identified the individual who insulted Islam yesterday by ridiculing the word 'lighad'. I understand that several police reports have been lodged ... at least one of those reports has been brought to my attention," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: Investigation into MCBA chief Shuhaily over KLIA incident ongoing
Article:
KULIM: Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail is leaving things entirely to the relevant agencies to investigate allegations of assault against Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
The home minister said the probe into the incident where Shuhaily was alleged to have assaulted two Special Branch policemen were continuing after the investigation paper (IP) was returned to police by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
He said the IP contained witness statements and other evidence.
"These are routine procedures. At this point in time, I will not comment other than to say I leave to the relevant authorities," he told reporters here.
It was reported yesterday that the A-GC had returned the IP to police for further action. (https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1550471/gc-returns-klia-probe-involving-mcba-chief-police)
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar had said among the aspects requiring review was the authenticity of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, along with several other related matters, before any decision could be finalised.
On another matter, Saifuddin declined comment when asked about a viral video which claimed a Rohingya man had entered Malaysia using a Bangladeshi passport.
"I do not want to respond to rumours or allegations. If there is a strong case and clear evidence, then I can respond."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget a government pledge to the people, says Anwar
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The 2027 Budget represents a "waad" (covenant) or pledge between the nation, its leaders and the people, which must be fulfilled with integrity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the 2027 Budget, the fifth under the unity government, was drawn up by a large team from the Finance Ministry and other ministries, taking into account the needs of various segments of society, from driving economic growth to addressing issues involving employment, wages and minimum income.
"We want to encourage all Malaysians from various walks of life to remember that this budget is not merely about managing finances, but must be a collective agreement bound by a covenant.
"This means a promise, pledge or oath between the nation, its leaders and the people.
"We have heard hundreds, and perhaps even more, views from various groups," Anwar said in a special interview on the 2027 Madani Budget broadcast by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) last night.
Anwar said the Madani government had considered the needs of all levels of society when formulating the 2027 Budget, with the aim of elevating the dignity and well-being of the people.
He said the government's plans under the 2027 Budget should ultimately ensure a more comfortable life for people from all walks of life in the future, while taking into account the challenges they faced.
[[nid:1552501]]
Anwar said the 2027 Budget focused not only on major priorities such as driving strong economic growth, but also on other concerns, including cat welfare, the welfare of gig workers and minimum income.
"The economy may be thriving, but the people may still be burdened. This is what I mean by a philosophy and an approach that takes a more holistic view, and that is what a budget should be.
"We have heard about the problems faced by gig workers, e-hailing and p-hailing riders. These were not issues 10 years ago. They are new developments," he said.
Anwar said the 2027 Budget also reflected the importance of managing the country properly and ensuring that its leaders remained committed to upholding their trust and responsibilities.
"This is a budget in which the nation upholds its trust, safeguards it as a responsibility and treats it as a covenant. It is a promise that must be fulfilled in all sincerity," he said.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat, allocating RM510 billion to improve the dignity and well-being of the people at all levels of society.
The 2027 Budget outlines eight key foundations, covering commitments to improve people's lives and an agenda to strengthen the nation's resilience and future.
When tabling the Supply Bill (2027 Budget) in the Dewan Rakyat, Anwar summed up this commitment as a "National Covenant", a promise that national progress must ultimately translate into a more dignified life for the people and strengthen Malaysia for future generations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget savings to ease cost-of-living pressures, says Anwar
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government will continue to prioritise prudent fiscal management under the 2027 Budget to channel savings back to the people and ease cost-of-living pressures, particularly among lower-income groups.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said savings generated through improved governance and efforts to curb leakages would be channelled back to the people, as the government sought to strengthen the country's finances without compromising assistance for those in need.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said that although Malaysia's inflation rate was around two per cent, among the lowest in the world, people continued to feel cost-of-living pressures due to rising prices of certain goods and services.
"When people ask why this could not have been done two years ago, we first had to resolve several issues. We needed to address debt, save and set priorities," he said in a special interview on the 2027 Budget aired on RTM tonight.
He said the government also needed to balance efforts to reduce debt and control spending with the need to increase allocations for critical sectors, including defence, housing for military and police personnel, and school facilities.
This approach was important to ensure every ringgit spent by the government delivered greater economic and social value to the people, he said.
Anwar said the government's fiscal space had improved through more disciplined financial management, but the savings had to be protected from being eroded again by leakages and wastage.
He said the stronger fiscal position enabled the government to provide assistance such as sports shoes for schoolchildren, as well as allowances and minimum-income support for smallholders and padi farmers.
"All this can be done when we manage our finances well and ensure government spending reaches the intended target groups," he said.
Anwar said the government's economic strategy also focused on investments in high-value sectors such as information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence (AI), but such development had to be accompanied by efforts to raise incomes and productivity.
"Investment, IT and AI are what we are trying to reach for in the sky, but being anchored on our values means looking at wages, the prices of goods, the needs of persons with disabilities (PwD) and children who lack basic facilities," he said, referring to the Budget 2027 theme, "Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values".
He said strong economic growth had to translate into quality jobs, higher wages and a narrower income gap, rather than being measured solely by gross domestic product (GDP) growth.
Anwar said the government would also continue to consider social and cultural development needs in its economic planning, including Islamic education and assistance for non-Muslim communities to maintain their places of worship.
He acknowledged that the 2027 Budget could not solve every economic problem, but stressed that the government's fiscal policy would prioritise easing the burden on groups most affected by financial pressures.
[[nid:1552491]]
Anwar also explained that some prices were influenced by external factors and global markets, citing the cost of phosphate fertiliser imported through the Strait of Hormuz amid the Middle East crisis.
He said fluctuations in commodity prices, logistics costs and disruptions to international supply chains could directly affect domestic prices, limiting the government's ability to control all prices directly.
However, the government could still ease price pressures by improving supply chains, expanding farmers' markets and increasing sales of goods through the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama), he said.
Anwar said assistance and facilities for the people would be provided according to the country's financial capacity, with a more targeted approach to prevent public resources from being wasted.
He cited the decision to maintain the subsidised RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 per litre despite rising global oil prices as an example of measures to protect household disposable income.
He said the oil price assumption used in the government's initial projections was US$70 per barrel, but this had risen to about US$110, while the RON95 petrol price remained at RM1.99 per litre.
Anwar said the decision reflected the need to balance the fiscal pressure of subsidies with the need to maintain stable transport costs and protect the people's purchasing power.
"Ultimately, in managing the national economy, the income and livelihoods of ordinary people are taken into consideration," he said.
He also said that the government would continue to formulate and implement policies based on the country's fiscal capacity, focusing on strengthening the economy, boosting productivity, curbing leakages and protecting those most affected by cost-of-living pressures.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled the 2027 Budget, themed "Reaching for the Sky, While Anchored on Our Values", with government expenditure totalling RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments and RM14.2 billion from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc) companies. The overall figure was RM510 billion, maintaining an expansionary fiscal policy.
The fifth Madani Budget aims to translate resilient economic growth into tangible benefits for the people through better wages, more efficient targeted assistance, stronger fiscal discipline and an accelerated push towards higher-value industries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget aims to improve quality of life, ensure social justice for all, says Anwar
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The 2027 Budget is designed to ensure a better quality of life and social justice for all Malaysians through a development approach that takes into account the needs of different groups, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government was not focused solely on headline figures and strategic sectors, but was also looking at the everyday needs of the people, including pet owners, persons with disabilities (PwD), gig workers and food and goods delivery riders.
"In any planning, the ultimate aim is to ensure the people's quality of life... we want a system that guarantees a comfortable and fair life for everyone," he said in a special interview on the 2027 Budget aired on RTM today.
However, Anwar said the 2027 Budget was not intended to solve every problem, but represented steps taken by the government to ease the burden on the people.
He said the government also needed to understand the challenges faced by rural communities, including padi farmers and fishermen, who continued to grapple with income constraints and limited access to certain facilities.
"In the cities, we do not have padi fields, but we know that people in padi-growing areas still face problems, while some coastal fishermen do not have licences... to issue licences, we need to consider the limited fish stocks," he said.
Anwar said the government therefore needed to find a balanced solution that would give fishermen some additional flexibility to earn a living without compromising the sustainability of fisheries resources.
[[nid:1552505]]
He said these efforts were part of a broader agenda to improve quality of life and strengthen social justice, rather than benefit any single group.
"All these issues fall under what we call quality of life and social justice, and this is not for one group, but for everyone... that is what we are trying to do to the best of our ability, God willing," he said.
Anwar said the Madani Economic Framework would continue to combine high-impact development aspirations with the people's basic needs, in line with the theme of 2027 Budget, "Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values".
He said the approach was important to ensure the country's economic progress was measured not only by macroeconomic achievements but also by the benefits felt in people's daily lives.
Anwar said the government would continue to listen to the people's views and concerns to ensure the policies and allocations under 2027 Budget addressed their current needs.
He stressed that every aspect of the budget should contribute to a more comfortable, fair and dignified life for all Malaysians.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027, with government expenditure totalling RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), comprising RM11 billion in public-private investments and RM14.2 billion from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc) companies.
This brings the overall 2027 Budget figure to RM510 billion, maintaining an expansionary fiscal policy.
The fifth Madani Budget aims to translate resilient economic growth into tangible benefits for the people through better wages, more efficient targeted assistance, stronger fiscal discipline and an accelerated push towards higher-value industries.
[[nid:1552504]]
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Special task force to probe RM350,000 bribe claims against MACC officer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has formed a special task force to review and reexamine allegations of corruption involving RM350,000 linked to a senior officer of the commission.
MACC said the matter had been investigated in 2018 but the case was closed as no offence was proven then.
However, following calls for action and the renewed circulation of the claims, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman ordered the immediate establishment of the special task force.
"This measure was taken to ensure that the MACC's integrity is upheld and to maintain public confidence in the commission," MACC said in a statement.
It said the matter was being taken seriously as such allegations could jeopardise the credibility of the commission.
MACC reminded all parties not to spread information that had yet to be verified.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
Article:
LIMA: Businessman Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores, who shares two of his names with notorious European dictators, has been elected the mayor of a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, according to local election data.
The 45-year-old won the race for mayor of Queropalca, a municipality in Peru's central Huanuco region, and will take office on January 1.
The candidate from the left-wing Ahora Nacion party obtained 229 votes out of a total of 663 votes in elections on October 4, according to the National Office of Electoral Processes.
His closest rival, the far-right candidate Gaspar Osorio, received 204 votes.
Flores, who works in the freight transportation business, previously belonged to Popular Force – the party of Peru's right-wing President Keiko Fujimori – until 2025, according to electoral authorities.
Despite the name being associated with Germany's World War II-era Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler, several candidates with the name have won elections in Peru.
In 2021, Peru elected physician Hitler Saavedra Casternoque to parliament for the centrist party Somos Peru.
In 2018, Hitler Alba Sanchez was voted in as mayor of the Andean district of Yungar, saying during his campaign that he was "the good Hitler."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jalaluddin denies plans for no-confidence motion against Negri Sembilan MB
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Jalaluddin Alias has denied plans to submit a motion of no confidence against Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim at the upcoming state legislative assembly sitting.
"Allegations that we want to bring a vote of no confidence against the menteri besar are simply not true," he said.
The denial follows media reports quoting sources claiming Negri Sembilan Umno was considering the motion, subject to approval from the party's central leadership.
The Negri Sembilan assembly sitting is scheduled for Nov 26, after being postponed from Oct 16 to align with the presentation of the state's 2027 Budget the following day.
Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on Aug 2 following the state election which saw Barisan Nasional win 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan 11, and Perikatan Nasional seven.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget balances cost-of-living relief with future growth
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The 2027 Budget strikes a balance between helping Malaysians cope with the rising cost of living and planning for the country's future economic growth, says Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Yusof Apdal.
"Personally, I think yesterday's budget was a very balanced one, as Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim took into consideration how we can help the people overcome the increasingly challenging cost of living due to the global situation.
"At the same time, it balances these efforts with plans for the country's future economic development," he told the media on the sidelines of a Kupi-Kupi Bah session at a hotel here.
The Lahad Datu member of parliament said the budget also supported efforts to develop Malaysia into a high-technology nation while ensuring its benefits reached the people.
On Sabah's allocation, Yusof said there was an increase from the previous year and expressed hope that the additional funding would benefit the people, particularly those facing various challenges.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim tabled a federal allocation of RM18.7 billion for Sabah, up from RM17.6 billion in 2026.
"We hope this increase can be put to good use, especially for the people who are dealing with various problems. Insya-Allah, additional allocations like this can help them," he said.
Earlier, in his speech, Yusof, a former deputy higher education minister, urged the media to explain the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan facilities announced in 2027 Budget to encourage Sabah students to pursue university education.
"Don't think about scholarships first. Take the PTPTN loan and enter university.
"Once you have registered, use the loan first. Along the way, if you get a scholarship, apply for it and convert the loan," he said.
He added that some students in Sabah might misunderstand the available options and give up on furthering their studies while waiting for scholarships.
Yusof said Budget 2027 also provided greater flexibility for PTPTN borrowers, with repayments to begin when their salaries reached RM2,500 and minimum monthly payments set at RM50.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Camera traps installed in Fraser's Hill to track tiger spotted there
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has installed four camera traps after receiving reports of a Malayan tiger roaming by the roadside along the Fraser's Hill route near Raub.
Pahang Perhilitan director Yusoff Shariff said his department received information regarding the incident about 9am yesterday.
"Four Perhilitan officers went to the location to conduct an investigation and install camera traps," he said when contacted.
He added that monitoring in the area will continue to gather further information regarding the presence of the tiger.
It was
reported
that several photographs depicting the animal's presence went viral on social media, sparking various reactions from the public.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget described as 'SME Budget'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) has described the 2027 Budget as an "SME Budget".
It also endorsed the declaration of 2027 as "Malaysia MSME Year" by Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong.
Samenta president Datuk William Ng said the budget placed micro, small and medium enterprises at the forefront of the nation's economic momentum.
He said the financing package and tax cut would provide direct cash flow relief and help businesses address core operating overheads.
He said the government's decision to exempt SMEs from the revised RM2,000 minimum wage proves that the 2027 Budget was formulated around the operational realities of small business owners.
The exemption applies to micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million.
Ng also endorsed the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry's ABCD Framework, which he said offered a targeted roadmap to scale the "missing middle".
He said the framework would enable local small businesses to modernise, integrate into high-value supply chains and compete regionally.
Describing itself as the country's oldest and largest SME association, Samenta said it would work closely with the minister and the ministry on ground-level implementation.
"The immediate priority is to ensure these budgetary initiatives, particularly financing facilities, digital automation support, and export market access, are disbursed rapidly with minimal red-tape so that the full benefits of this 'SME Budget' are felt across our business community," Ng said in a statement.
One of the
key announcements
under the 2027 Budget is that total loan facilities and financing guarantees will increase from RM50 billion to RM57 billion next year, while income tax rates for micro, small and medium enterprises will be cut by one percentage point.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim also announced that the
minimum wage
would be raised from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL Car Free Morning cancelled due to haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur Car Free Morning (KLCFM) programme, scheduled to take place at Dataran DBKL here tomorrow, has been cancelled due to the haze.
The KLCFM Working Committee said the decision was made after taking into account the risks participants could face from haze exposure, particularly while engaging in outdoor physical activities.
"The event scheduled for Sunday, Oct 11, at Dataran DBKL has been cancelled.
"The safety, health and well-being of all participants have always been the organisers' priority," it said in a statement.
The organisers also apologised for any inconvenience caused and expressed their appreciation for the public's support and understanding.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
Article:
ALOR SETAR: All educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring areas in the state were recorded below 100 as of 2pm today.
The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this is, however, subject to further directives from the Education Ministry and relevant authorities.
"The Kedah JPN expresses its appreciation for the concern and decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, regarding the importance of safeguarding the safety, health and welfare of students and education personnel following the haze affecting several areas in the country.
"The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual," the statement said.
The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.
"Schools should also pay close attention to students and education personnel experiencing health problems, particularly those who are sensitive to air quality conditions, and take appropriate action if any students or education personnel show signs of ill health.
"The Kedah JPN will continue to monitor developments in the haze situation and coordinate action with all District Education Offices and educational institutions based on the latest readings and directives from the authorities," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Hospital outsourcing scheme to cover more patients, specialities
Article:
IPOH: The Health Ministry will expand its Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme (HSOP) to cover more patients and potentially new specialities following an increase in its allocation to RM200 million under the 2027 Budget.
Its deputy director-general of health (medical), Datuk Dr Mohd Azman Yaacob, said the additional RM56 million would enable the ministry to refer more patients to private hospitals for treatment.
He said the ministry was also studying the possibility of extending the programme to other specialities, including oncology.
"HSOP aims to reduce waiting times and ease congestion at government hospitals.
"We will increase the number of patients who can receive treatment at private hospitals and explore expanding the programme to other specialities," he said.
Dr Azman was speaking to reporters after attending a public-private partnership initiative involving cataract surgery at Perak Community Specialist Hospital (PCSH) here today.
Also present were Perak Chinese Maternity Association secretary-general Datuk Lim Si Boon and Perak Health Department director Datuk Dr Feisul Idzwan Mustapha.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced under the 2027 Budget that RM200 million would be allocated to outsource patients' treatment to other hospitals to reduce waiting times, particularly at urban hospitals.
Introduced in 2024, HSOP currently covers nephrology, cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, paediatric cardiology and radiology.
Under the programme, patients requiring medical imaging services, including ultrasound scans, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) scans, can be referred to participating private healthcare facilities.
The programme also covers selected cardiac procedures, including angiograms and coronary artery bypass surgery.
Dr Azman said the initiative was particularly important in reducing waiting times for medical imaging services, with patients at government hospitals sometimes having to wait between three and six months for CT scans.
He said private hospitals participating in the programme had to agree to the rates offered before accepting referrals from government hospitals.
"Patients will receive the required treatment and follow-up care at private facilities before returning to their referring government hospitals to continue their treatment," he said.
He added that HSOP did not mean patients would receive treatment entirely free of charge.
"Patients will continue to pay the applicable charges imposed at government hospitals, while the government will cover the remaining treatment costs through the programme.
"For example, if the actual cost of treatment at a private hospital is RM3,000, patients would pay the applicable government hospital charges, while the government would cover the balance through HSOP," he said.
On the cataract surgery initiative, Dr Azman said between 1,500 and 2,000 patients were awaiting surgery at Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun here.
He said the ministry would continue to explore partnerships with private healthcare providers beyond the Klang Valley to help patients nationwide receive treatment sooner.
"With initiatives such as this, we can ensure these procedures are carried out earlier, allowing patients to receive treatment more promptly.
"We will continue to explore opportunities to work with private hospitals and specialist centres, including PCSH, to sustain these initiatives.
"We have already established similar collaborations with other parties in the Klang Valley. However, these efforts should not be confined to the Klang Valley, as many more Malaysians need timely surgery to improve their quality of life," he said.
Meanwhile, Lim said the collaboration with PCSH involved 40 cataract operations costing about RM250,000, with the expenses borne by the hospital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: El-Sisi invites Sultan Ibrahim, Anwar to visit Egypt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt.
The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today.
"It speaks much to the depth and strength of the relations between our two countries," he said at a joint press conference with Anwar at the Seri Perdana Complex, Putrajaya today.
El-Sisi also touched on cooperation with Malaysia in key areas including energy and renewable energy, manufacturing, electronics, agriculture, and food industries.
He said both countries were seeking to translate their strong bilateral relations into tangible outcomes, with energy, manufacturing, electronics, agriculture, and food industries identified as key areas for expanded cooperation.
The president added that the potential for collaboration was significant, provided both countries combined their capabilities with strong political will and commitment.
"I believe that the understanding, the mutual trust, and the reciprocal political will of both parties shall enhance our cooperation and take our relationship to a whole new level," he said.
In a joint statement today, Anwar and El-Sisi announced the elevation of bilateral relations between Malaysia and Egypt to a Strategic Partnership.
"Under this framework, both leaders reaffirmed their shared interest in accelerating efforts in building a more dynamic and resilient partnership across all sectors, thereby jointly promoting global prosperity and stability.
"Both leaders acknowledged the importance of regular dialogue through existing bilateral institutional mechanisms and in this regard, agreed to convene the second Joint Commission Meeting (JCM) and the second Bilateral Consultations (BC) at the earliest opportunity," the statement read.
Meanwhile, El-Sisi said he and Anwar also discussed al-Azhar University's instrumental role in the teaching and practice of moderate Islam.
"Egypt is receiving students, males and females, from all over the world, especially from Malaysia, which we are really proud of. They are very bright young men and women, and we are proud of them and proud of everybody who comes to seek education and knowledge in Egypt.
"We are not only ready to increase the number of Malaysian students, but also to exchange scholars and preachers, so that they can disseminate moderation and tolerance of Islam in this beautiful country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teenager drowns at Kuantan beach
Article:
KUANTAN: A trip to the beach turned tragic when a 16-year-old boy drowned at Pantai Sepat along Jalan Kuantan-Pekan here today.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the body Mohamad Raiyan Khairul Anuar was found about 50m from where he was last seen in the water.
"The department received a report of the incident at 9.56am, and despatched six firemen from the Kuantan station.
"Four divers from the department's Water Rescue Unit in Kuantan and Pekan were later deployed to assist in the search. The victim was subsequently found and pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel," he said in a statement.
Salahuddin said the victim's remains were handed over to police for further action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: 28 areas nationwide record unhealthy air quality at 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor and Selangor remained among the states most affected by the haze, with 28 areas nationwide recording unhealthy air quality as of 5pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), eight air quality monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, followed by four in Selangor.
In Johor, Tangkak recorded the highest API reading at 185, followed by Larkin and Pasir Gudang (182), Segamat and Batu Pahat (176), Kluang (173), Kota Tinggi (171) and Pengerang (170).
In Selangor, Shah Alam recorded an API reading of 159, followed by Johan Setia (157), Petaling Jaya (155) and Klang (147).
The other 16 monitoring stations recording unhealthy API readings were located in Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, Putrajaya and Sarawak.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 169, while Batu Muda recorded 160. Putrajaya recorded 161. In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded an API reading of 172, followed by Nilai (168) and Port Dickson (160).
In Pahang, Rompin recorded 170, followed by Balok Baru in Kuantan (153) and Indera Mahkota (152). In Perak, Tasek in Ipoh recorded an API reading of 169, followed by Pegoh in Ipoh (166) and Tanjung Malim (165).
In Melaka, Alor Gajah, Bukit Rambai and Melaka Town each recorded an API reading of 165, while Kuching in Sarawak recorded 153.
Meanwhile, 40 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings, according to APIMS data. No areas recorded good air quality.
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: El-Sisi departs after 2-day state visit to Malaysia
Article:
SEPANG: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The special aircraft carrying El-Sisi took off from the Bunga Raya Complex (BRC) at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 4.38pm.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin were present to bid farewell to the Egyptian leader.
Earlier, El-Sisi inspected a guard of honour mounted by officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment, led by Captain Muhammad Nafis Norshid.
A cultural performance by the Istana Budaya arts troupe was also held to mark his departure, showcasing Malaysia's rich cultural heritage through traditional dances and musical performances featuring traditional instruments.
The visit was El-Sisi's first to Malaysia since he assumed office in June 2014.
During the visit, El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara, where Sultan Ibrahim granted an audience to the Egyptian president and his delegation. The King also witnessed a presentation of royal tokens of appreciation at Dewan Seri Maharaja.
Sultan Ibrahim subsequently hosted a state banquet at the Grand Banquet Hall in honour of El-Sisi and the Egyptian government delegation.
El-Sisi and Anwar then held a four-eyed meeting at the Seri Perdana Complex, marking a significant step towards elevating Malaysia-Egypt relations to a strategic partnership after more than six decades of diplomatic ties.
The meeting provided an opportunity for both leaders to review bilateral cooperation, explore new areas of collaboration and exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest.
The two countries also exchanged four memoranda of understanding (MoUs) covering women's empowerment, higher education, tourism and investment. The exchange was witnessed by Anwar and El-Sisi.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to El-Sisi for personally facilitating Malaysia's humanitarian assistance to Palestinians, including efforts to bring injured victims from Gaza to Malaysia for medical treatment.
The prime minister said Egypt had provided significant support for Malaysia's humanitarian initiatives, with coordination facilitated directly through the Egyptian president's office and the country's military intelligence.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia's seventh-largest trading partner in Africa, with total bilateral trade valued at RM3.08 billion (US$720 million).
Malaysia's exports to Egypt amounted to RM2.55 billion (US$600 million), while imports totalled RM530 million (US$120 million).
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade rose 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$870 million).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Black river waters, dead fish leave Raub villagers worried
Article:
RAUB: Frustration is mounting among villagers in Kampung Sungai Pasu after Sungai Gali, a popular fishing spot, turned black and began emitting a foul smell.
Various species of dead fish have been spotted floating downstream, raising fears of serious water pollution.
Sungai Pasu village headman Mohd Zaidi Hashim said the river, which is usually brownish, turned black several days ago, with dead fish floating on the surface.
"Something is not right with the water... a farmer upstream noticed that the water had turned black on Wednesday but did not suspect anything until various fish species were found dead yesterday.
"Sungai Gali is a popular spot for villagers to fish and cast their nets, but the strong stench has kept them away. The dead fish include baung (catfish) and tilan (spiny eels)... even tilan known for its ability to survive in poor water conditions have been found dead," he told the
New Straits Times
today.
Zaidi said the pollution was believed to have entered Sungai Lampan before spreading downstream to other rivers along the waterway, including Sungai Gali.
"We are worried that the dark colour could be caused by toxic waste, which might affect the livelihoods of villagers who depend on fish caught in the river. So far, the discoloured water has reached rivers in Kampung Kuala Gali and Pia.
"Everyone is concerned because this is the first time the water has changed colour," he said, adding that the Department of Environment (DoE) had collected water samples yesterday.
Earlier, Dong assemblyman Datuk Fadzli Mohamad Kamal said Sungai Gali and Sungai Lampan had been
severely polluted
, threatening river ecosystems and disrupting villagers' daily lives.
He called for immediate action to prevent further damage to the rivers and stop the pollution from spreading to other waterways.
Meanwhile, villager Ahmad Abdullah, 40, said residents usually cast their nets below the bridge in Kampung Sungai Pasu, where fish were abundant, including some exceptionally large baung.
"The polluted river and dead fish have kept anglers away. I do not think anyone will return to cast their nets until the authorities confirm the source of the pollution," he said.
Pahang DoE director Zakaria Ahmad said water samples had been collected and were awaiting analysis by the Chemistry Department.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Turkiye social media ban for under-15s takes effect Nov 1
Article:
ISTANBUL: Turkiye on Saturday formally declared a ban on the use of social media for under-15s, scheduled to come into effect on November 1.
It has joined a growing number of countries legislating to protect children and teenagers from the harmful effects of online platforms.
The official state journal published the decision following the adoption of a law by parliament in April.
It stipulates that social media providers must "take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement" protections for young people.
"No service likely to produce an addictive effect in children may be offered."
Countries including Australia have introduced restrictions on social media for children and others such as Britain and France are pushing to do the same.
They aim to protect children from digital risks such as screen addiction, lack of sleep, bullying and eating disorders.
Rights groups have complained of restrictions on freedom of expression in Turkey targeting LGBTQ communities, the media and the political opposition. Numerous social media accounts have been blocked in recent weeks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiger spotted roaming by roadside near Fraser's Hill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malayan tiger was spotted roaming along the road shoulder near Fraser's Hill heading towards Kuala Kubu Baru (KKB), Selangor.
The sighting was shared in a viral post on Threads by the account 'peann999', accompanied by two photos showing the wild animal standing at the roadside near the forest.
According to the post, the tiger was spotted near the GS Gap Chorocco trek area, about one kilometre from the Fraser's Hill junction heading towards KKB.
The user issued a warning to all road users and hikers using the route.
"Do not stop, do not open your windows. Do not get out of the car. The tiger was spotted roaming by the roadside," the post read.
Meanwhile, when contacted, the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) said it is investigating the tiger's presence in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India detains 'cockroach' leaders ahead of election protest
Article:
NEW DELHI: Indian police detained the head of the satirical "cockroach" online movement on Saturday, the group said, ahead of a major protest against the Election Commission that triggered strict security measures.
The demonstration, due to take place in New Delhi, is the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital, the youth-led CJP said in a social media post, while television networks aired footage showing uniformed police aboard the plane.
"It's official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship," Arvind Kejriwal of the opposition Aam Aadmi Party said in a statement.
"Arresting cockroaches straight off their flight shows an unprecedented level of fear."
Opposition parties and other critics say the voter-roll revision could disenfranchise millions of voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety, saying the "special intensive revision" was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
Delhi has been under a strict security clampdown since Friday, with tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed to stop those seeking to reach the main protest site in the heart of the city.
Authorities have closed dozens of metro stations, cancelled several trains coming to Delhi and temporarily shut down mobile internet around the protest site.
AFP reporters saw police chasing down protesters on Saturday and hauling them into vehicles around central Delhi.
More than 200 protesters have been detained so far, local media reports said.
Media outlets, including the Scroll and Newslaundry, said their journalists had also been detained.
AFP was unable to reach police for comment on the reported detentions.
The protests are widely seen as a reprise of the "cockroach" movement's mass mobilisation in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.
This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign from his post.
- 'Choking the city' -
The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office.
Opposition parties have long alleged that legitimate voters are being struck off voter lists in India, the world's largest democracy with 1.4 billion people.
But the issue blew up last month when the Indian Express reported that key decisions linked to the revision were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners.
The ECI, a constitutional body, says all its decisions were unanimous and legally valid.
Sanjeev Takshak, one of a handful of protesters who managed to reach close to the protest site on Saturday, said he had come there out of "a sense of duty."
"The state is choking the entire city to prevent people from expressing their opinion," Takshak, a lawyer, said.
"It is absolutely not fair," the 42-year-old told AFP.
Delhi Police said they had taken the steps to ensure law and order.
"People should be able to raise their concerns peacefully," the force said in a statement. "Our responsibility is to create the conditions in which they can do that safely, while keeping the city functioning."
Amnesty International denounced the "lockdown-like restrictions."
"Peaceful protesters must be able to demand accountability from those in power without facing intimidation, arbitrary detention, or sweeping restrictions on their freedoms," it said in a statement.
The voter list overhaul, which began in 2025, has led to more than 133 million names being excluded from draft rolls.
The exclusions include duplicate entries and people found to have died.
The poll body said the exercise identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent "foreign illegal immigrants" from casting ballots.
Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalised and minority communities.
Members of Modi's party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Egypt ink four MoUs, strengthen bilateral cooperation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia and Egypt signed four memoranda of understanding (MoU) today to strengthen bilateral cooperation in empowering women, higher education, tourism and investments.
The exchanges of all four MoUs were witnessed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi.
The first MoU involved the empowerment of woman, between Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri and Egyptian Foreign Affairs, Emigration and Expatriates Minister Dr Badr Ahmed Mohamed Abdelatty.
The second, involving higher education, was between Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and Abdelatty.
For tourism, the MoU was between Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing and Abdelatty.
The final MoU was between the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) and Egypt's General Authority for Investment and Free Zones.
The exchange of documents for this MoU was between Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Egypt's Investment and Foreign Trade Minister Dr Mohamed Farid Saleh.
El-Sisi is in Malaysia for a two-day state visit on the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
He was earlier
accorded a state welcome
at Istana Negara.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Unauthorised oil blending could tarnish Malaysia’s global image, experts warn
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Oil blending activities must obtain written approval from the Customs director-general where required under the relevant regulations, and be backed by complete documentation to ensure legal compliance and transparent transactions, an expert said.
Maritime, Customs and cross-border trade policy and law expert Madzli Harun said every activity involving the import, storage, blending and re-export of oil must be carried out within the scope of the licence and the conditions set by the authorities.
He said blending could alter a product’s composition and specifications, so clear records were needed to verify quantities, cargo movements and the condition of the product before and after the process.
Related documents such as contracts, bills of lading and cargo manifests must be aligned to ensure the information declared matched the actual transactions and the condition of the goods, he said.
“If a premises is only approved for storage, any additional activities such as blending or changing a product’s grade must be scrutinised based on the scope of the licence and the regulations in force.
“Operators must ensure written approval is obtained when required, and that all activities are recorded accurately,” he said at a forum titled “Strengthening Malaysia’s Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia’s Regulatory Landscape”, organised by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd in collaboration with Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT).
Madzli said incomplete documentation, or discrepancies between records and the actual condition of the cargo, could raise questions over the declaration of goods, regulatory compliance and tax treatment.
A thorough audit was also important to ensure the volumes of oil received, stored, blended and exported could be identified and matched against the relevant documents, he added.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said responsible petroleum cargo management was not merely an operational matter, but also a question of protecting the country’s interests and ensuring future generations inherited a maritime industry built on transparency, safety and accountability.
In cross-border trade, he said, determining the origin of goods and their eligibility for treatment under free trade agreements must be based on the rules of origin and the relevant supporting documents.
As such, industry operators must ensure every transaction complied with the set conditions, while the authorities must have sufficient records to assess compliance levels and tax implications, he said.
He said clear controls over blending, including approval requirements and proper documentation, were key to preserving the integrity of the Customs system and reducing the risk of disputes between industry players and the authorities.
Meanwhile, maritime industry expert Nazery Khalid said oil blending carried out without approval, monitoring, compliance with standards and proper documentation must be taken seriously, as incidents could threaten health and safety and undermine the integrity of the authorities responsible for monitoring such activities.
He said if such incidents occurred, questions would arise over compliance with safety procedures, the effectiveness of monitoring and the enforcement of regulations on oil blending.
Approval, documentation oversight and compliance with operating conditions must be given close attention to ensure every activity was carried out in a controlled manner, in line with the set regulations as well as international standards and best practices, he said.
He said weaknesses and a lack of integrity in documentation, supervision and enforcement could not only pose risks to the public and the environment, but also erode the confidence of industry players, trading partners and the international community in the transparency of Malaysia’s cargo-handling regulatory system.
“Inconsistent and inaccurate cargo documents such as the bill of lading and manifest should not be taken lightly, especially for liquid cargo such as petroleum products and palm oil. They could open the door to various forms of misconduct that could harm health and the environment.
“If this situation is not addressed promptly and comprehensively, it could undermine public confidence in the integrity of the industry concerned and damage the country’s image on the international stage,” he said.
At the end of the session, Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said responsible petroleum cargo management was not merely an operational matter, but also a question of protecting the country’s interests and ensuring future generations inherited a maritime industry built on transparency, safety and accountability.

Title: Better roads, stronger pitch: MB sees Budget 2027 lifting Negeri Sembilan’s investment appeal
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 10 — The provision of better infrastructure facilities is expected to enhance Negeri Sembilan’s attractiveness as an investment destination, in line with the ongoing development of Malaysia Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0).
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the construction of a new road from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Bandar Enstek was among the key infrastructure facilities that would support development in the area, while facilitating movement and improving accessibility.
“Alhamdulillah, Negeri Sembilan is not being left behind in benefiting from Budget 2027 announced yesterday. Among the initiatives are a new road from KLIA to Bandar Enstek, as well as the upgrading of Jalan Pajam-Nilai-Salak. The new road will also complement the development of MVV 2.0.
“This is significant and a good selling point for the state government, while giving Negeri Sembilan an advantage in attracting more investors,” he told reporters after the close of the Negeri Sembilan Malaysia Property Expo (Mapex) today, which was also attended by state Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) chairman Datuk Hoo Kim See.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027, said the Madani government would complete the development of MVV 2.0 with infrastructure projects including the new KLIA-Bandar Enstek road, the upgrading of Jalan Pajam-Nilai-Salak and the implementation of the Klang Valley Dual Track 2 project.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the construction of the Rembau Integrated Health Complex would also benefit the state by expanding healthcare facilities for the public, particularly as several existing hospitals in Negeri Sembilan were facing problems, including a shortage of beds.
He said the facility was important to increase the state’s healthcare service capacity and complement the government’s efforts to improve healthcare facilities to meet the needs of a growing population.
He also expressed hope that initiatives announced under Budget 2027 would be implemented according to schedule to ensure the people could enjoy the intended benefits as planned.
Ismail said smooth implementation within the stipulated timeframe was crucial, as delays or problems with project execution could prompt complaints from the public, who had high expectations following the government’s announcements.
“What matters is not just the announcement of expenditure, but also how it is implemented. Sometimes, we announce a lot, but implementation gets held up and does not proceed on time. This will create problems for the people who have placed their hopes in these announcements,” he said.
He said the state government would continue to facilitate and cooperate through the relevant departments to ensure the projects could be implemented smoothly, allowing the people to benefit within the stipulated timeframe. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Budget 2027 will balance fiscal discipline with cost-of-living relief
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — The government will continue to focus on prudent fiscal management in Budget 2027 to return benefits to the people and reduce cost-of-living pressures, especially for low-income households, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The prime minister said that savings from improved governance and efforts to curb leakages will be redirected to the people, in line with the need to strengthen the country’s financial position without compromising assistance to those in need.
Anwar, also the finance minister, said although Malaysia’s inflation rate is around two per cent, one of the lowest in the world, the public still feels cost-of-living pressures due to rising prices of goods and certain services.
“When people ask why this could not be done two years ago, we had to resolve several issues first. We had to address debt, be prudent, and set priorities,” he said in a special Madani Budget 2027 interview aired by RTM tonight.
Anwar noted that the government must balance the need to reduce debt and curb spending with the requirement to increase allocations for critical sectors such as defence, housing for service members and police, and school facilities.
According to him, this approach is important to ensure every ringgit the government spends delivers greater economic and social value for the people.
Anwar said the government’s fiscal space has improved through more disciplined financial management, but these savings must be safeguarded from erosion by leakages and waste.
He noted that a stronger fiscal position enables the government to provide assistance such as sports shoes for schoolchildren, as well as allowances and minimum income support for rubber smallholders and paddy farmers.
“This can all be achieved if we manage finances well and ensure that government expenditure truly reaches the targeted groups,” he stressed.
The prime minister said the government’s economic strategy also focuses on investments in high-value sectors such as information technology and artificial intelligence (AI), but these developments must be accompanied by measures to boost people’s income and productivity.
“Investments, IT, and AI are the things (referencing Budget 2027’s theme) we are ‘reaching for in the skies while anchored on our values’, meaning looking at issues like salaries, the price of goods, the needs of people with disabilities, and children who do not have access to basic facilities,” he said.
Anwar said solid economic growth must translate into quality job opportunities, higher wages, and reduced income inequality, and should not be measured solely by the gross domestic product growth rate.
He said the government would also continue to take into account the needs of social and cultural development in economic planning, including Islamic education training and aid to non-Muslim communities to maintain places of worship.
He acknowledged that Budget 2027 cannot solve all economic problems, but emphasised that the government’s fiscal policy would prioritise easing the burdens on the groups most affected by financial pressures.
In addition, Anwar explained that external factors and global markets influence part of the price of goods, for example, the cost of imported phosphate fertiliser via the Hormuz Strait following the crisis in West Asia.
According to him, fluctuations in commodity prices, logistics costs, and disruptions in international supply chains can directly impact domestic prices, limiting the government’s ability to control all prices.
Nevertheless, he said the government can still reduce price pressures by streamlining the supply chain, expanding farmers’ markets, and increasing sales of goods through the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority.
Therefore, Anwar said the government would provide assistance and facilities based on the country’s financial capacity, with a more targeted approach to ensure public resources are not wasted.
As an example, he cited the decision to maintain subsidised RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre, even as global oil prices rise, as a measure to protect household disposable income.
He said the oil price used in the government’s initial projections was US$70 per barrel, but it rose to about US$110 per barrel, while RON95 petrol remained at RM1.99 per litre.
The decision, he said, reflects the government’s need to balance fiscal pressures from subsidies with the need to maintain stable transportation costs and the public’s purchasing power.
“Ultimately, in managing the national economy, the income and livelihoods of ordinary people become the measuring standards,” he said.
Anwar also emphasised that the government would continue to implement policies based on the country’s fiscal capacity, focusing on strengthening the economy, boosting productivity, reducing leakages, and protecting those most affected by cost-of-living pressures.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled Budget 2027 with the theme “Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values,” with government allocations amounting to RM459.8 billion, plus RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs); RM11 billion in public-private investments; and RM14.2 billion in investments by Federal Statutory Bodies and the Minister of Finance (Incorporated), resulting in Budget 2027 as an expansionary fiscal policy of RM510 billion.
The Fifth Madani Budget aims to translate resilient economic growth into tangible benefits for the people through higher wages, more efficient targeted support, stronger fiscal discipline, and aggressive steps toward higher-value industries. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says reduced waste and leakages created room for more Budget 2027 aid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Budget 2027 is the result of good national financial management, with the savings achieved now being returned to the people rather than enjoyed only by certain groups, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had to resolve the country’s financial priorities first before gaining a greater capacity to channel savings to the people.
“That is why people ask me, why couldn’t this be done two years ago? We resolved issues according to priority, fixing what is most important first.
“Money must be saved; do not be wasteful, do not lose it, and do not allow leakages... now that it has accumulated, we can return it to the people, not to ministers’ allowances,” he said in the Madani Budget 2027 Special Interview here today.
Anwar said good governance practices allowed the government to provide various forms of assistance and initiatives to the people, including the provision of sports shoes and aid for rubber smallholders and padi farmers.
He said this approach is the foundation for strengthening governance, which allows welfare initiatives to be implemented in stages according to the country’s financial capacity.
The prime minister said the government previously had to focus on debt management and urgent needs, including school facilities and housing for military and police personnel.
He said the savings achieved have now given the government some extra room to increase assistance for the people, but the effort must be accompanied by continuous financial discipline.
“And now, I say, we have a little more capacity. But on the condition that we do not allow leakages to recur,” he added.
When tabling Budget 2027 yesterday, Anwar announced increased allocations for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistances to RM16 billion from RM15 billion, with all STR recipients receiving up to RM150 a month or RM1,800 a year.
Additionally, Malaysians aged 18 and above who do not receive the STR will receive the Madani SARA of RM100 twice, namely before Aidilfitri and in conjunction with the country’s 70th National Day.
The prime minister said both initiatives will benefit up to nine million STR recipients and 13 million Malaysians, including the middle-income group (M40).
The Early Schooling Aid has also been increased to RM200 from RM150 this year, with an RM1 billion allocation benefiting 5.3 million students.
The government will also channel a one-off special financial assistance of RM1,000 to 38,000 taxi and rental car drivers, as well as 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide, following the revenue generated from the sale of ‘H’ special registration plates.
