The assistance will be disbursed next week as part of measures to return the revenue to the people. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 more than numbers, says Anwar — it is a promise to the people
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that Budget 2027 is a covenant between the country and its leadership and the people, which must be implemented with full trust and integrity.
The finance minister said the Fifth Madani Budget, formulated by a large team under the Ministry of Finance and other ministries, took into account the needs of various segments of society, ranging from driving economic growth to addressing issues concerning employment, wages and minimum income
“We want to remind all Malaysians from various walks of life that this budget is not merely about managing finances, but must be an agreement bound by a covenant.
“This means a promise, pledge or oath between the country, its leadership and the people. So, we listened to hundreds, and perhaps even more, views from various groups,” he said in the Special Madani Budget 2027 Interview aired by Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) tonight.
Anwar said the Madani government under his leadership had always considered all levels of society when formulating Budget 2027, themed “Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values”, while seeking to uphold the dignity and well-being of the people.
The prime minister added that whatever plans implemented by the government under Budget 2027 would ultimately ensure a better quality of life for various segments of society in the future, while taking into account all the challenges faced by the people.
He said Budget 2027 not only focused on major matters such as driving high economic growth, but also extended to issues such as cat welfare, as well as the welfare of gig workers and minimum income.
“The economy may be thriving, but the people may still be burdened. So, this is what I call a philosophy, an approach that takes a more holistic view, and that is essentially what a budget is.
“We have heard about the problems faced by gig workers, e-hailing and p-hailing workers. These are things that did not exist 10 years ago. They are new issues,” he said.
Anwar also explained that Budget 2027 was the result of how the country was being managed well, with the highest leadership always upholding its trust and responsibility.
“This is a budget where the country upholds its trust, safeguards it as a trust, and treats it as a covenant. It is a promise that must be fulfilled in earnest,” he said.
Yesterday, Anwar tabled Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, allocating RM510 billion to uphold the dignity and well-being of the people at all levels.
Budget 2027 outlines eight key pillars, encompassing commitments ranging from improving the people’s quality of life to strengthening the country’s resilience and future.
When tabling the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027, Anwar summed up the commitment as the “National Covenant” — a pledge that the country’s progress would ultimately translate into a more dignified life for the people and strengthen Malaysia for future generations. — Bernama

Title: Grieving mother haunted by memories of her three children killed in Pontian accident
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The mother of the three siblings who tragically died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong here, admits that she still finds it difficult to look at her children’s clothes and school bags as they serve as painful reminders of them.
Julaiha Munaji, 44, said the simultaneous loss of Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha Norlizan, 8, is the heaviest trial she and her family have ever faced.
She shared that the loss of her youngest child, Puteri Naufa, is felt the most because the only daughter among her six children was exceptionally close to her.
“I have six children, five boys and one girl. For years, my husband and I prayed for a daughter, but I was only blessed to have her with me for eight years.
“Even though I lost her two days ago, I accept it with a quiet heart and am grateful for the chance to raise her, even if it was only for a short time,” she told Bernama when met at her home in Kampung Parit Haji Siraj today.
Julaiha said among the things she misses the most is her daily routine of preparing breakfast and packed meals for her children before starting the day.
She added that she can still vividly picture the playful antics of her three children in the yard every evening, memories that are hard to forget.
“It will probably take time for me to get used to this loss. Losing even one child is heavy enough, but losing three all at once is unbearable,” she said.
Last Thursday, the three siblings died after the motorcycle they were riding collided with a lorry on Jalan Parit Haji Sirat, Kayu Ara Pasong at around 7:20 am, just after returning from Sekolah Kebangsaan Parit Sapran.
At the time, Nor Daniel Aiman was on his way back after taking his two younger siblings to the school to inform them that classes were canceled due to deteriorating air quality caused by haze.
Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Moin Hussain reported that two of the pillion riders died at the scene, while the motorcycle rider passed away while on the way to Pontian Hospital.
All schools in Johor were closed last Thursday and Friday due to the declining air quality, affecting more than 1,000 schools and approximately 600,000 students. — Bernama

Title: Melaka tourist spots remain busy despite unhealthy API readings
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 10 — Tourist spots around Banda Hilir here continue to draw local and foreign visitors despite Melaka recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings since Thursday due to the haze.
A Bernama check at the Stadthuys and Jonker Walk found that tourists were still visiting the popular attractions, while souvenir and handicraft shops remained open as usual.
However, few tourists and traders were seen wearing face masks to protect themselves from the effects of unhealthy air quality.
Asmah Zulkifli, 66, from Kuala Lumpur, said the haze had not deterred her and several friends from visiting tourist attractions, including the Stadthuys, after attending a friend’s wedding reception in Bukit Katil here.
“If not for the wedding, we wouldn’t have come to Melaka. Since we are here, we decided to drop by Banda Hilir.
“Alhamdulillah, even though it is hazy, this area is still attracting many visitors and remains lively,” said the former civil servant, who will return to Kuala Lumpur tomorrow afternoon.
She said they planned to visit several other tourist attractions if the haze did not reach hazardous levels.
Trishaw peddler Muhammad Azhan Fikry Munawir, 28, said tourism activities in the area remained lively, with local and foreign tour groups continuing to visit.
“Perhaps, to the public, the impact of the haze is not like COVID. Besides, tourist areas in Melaka are still operating as usual.
“It is just that trishaw peddlers have to be more careful because we spend longer periods outdoors and are more exposed to the health effects,” said Muhammad Azhan, who has worked as a trishaw peddler for 10 years.
Meanwhile, souvenir trader Amalina Zulkifli, 34, said the haze had not deterred tourists from visiting the UNESCO World Heritage Site.
“Alhamdulillah, there are many tourists around this area today. Only yesterday there were slightly fewer, perhaps because it was a working day and the API reading was higher than today,” she said.
Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed that API readings in Melaka had declined compared with yesterday but remained in the unhealthy range as of 5 pm today, with Alor Gajah and Bandaraya Melaka each recording 164, while Bukit Rambai recorded 163. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid wants tahfiz graduates equipped for careers in technology, engineering and medicine
Article:
BANGI, Oct 10 — Tahfiz graduates should have wider opportunities to pursue higher education and professional careers in fields such as technology, engineering and medicine to meet the country’s evolving workforce needs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said tahfiz education should go beyond Quran memorisation by equipping graduates with the knowledge, skills and qualifications needed to pursue a broader range of careers.
“My principle is simple. Tahfiz graduates should not have to choose between religion and their ambitions. They should be given the opportunity to deepen their religious knowledge while acquiring the skills and qualifications needed for professional careers,” he said at the 10th Huffaz Nusantara Permata Al-Quran Convocation at the German-Malaysian Institute here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who chairs the National Tahfiz Council, said advances in artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and high technology made it increasingly important for tahfiz graduates to develop skills that would enable them to compete across various sectors.
As such, he said tahfiz education must also keep pace with the country’s human capital needs by providing more pathways to universities, technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions, industry and professional fields.
Achieving this would require cooperation among the government, tahfiz institutions, universities and industry to ensure graduates had clear opportunities to progress after completing their studies.
“Tahfiz graduates must not be left to find their own way after graduation. The ecosystem must help them move on to the next stage,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts to strengthen tahfiz education included enhancing the National Tahfiz Education Policy, developing the Malaysian Tahfiz Recognition Standard and strengthening pathways through the Malaysian Tahfiz Certificate to broaden graduates’ education and career options.
He also welcomed the increased allocation for Islamic affairs, pondok schools, tahfiz institutions and people’s religious schools under Budget 2027, as well as improved allowances for religious teachers and mosque personnel
“This reflects the government’s commitment to supporting those involved in Islamic religious affairs, and is a positive development that deserves the support of all parties,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, announced that the allocation for Islamic affairs had been increased to RM3.1 billion from RM2.6 billion this year. — Bernama

Title: Lights on: Works Department to extend streetlight operating hours during haze
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The Public Works Department (JKR) will extend the operating hours of its streetlights by up to two hours during haze conditions to help improve visibility for road users.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the measure, implemented through JKR’s Electrical Engineering Branch, was prompted by haze conditions that had reduced visibility and increased the risk of accidents.
He said streetlights using timer systems currently typically operated from 7 pm to 7 am.
“Each streetlight has a timer setting that can be adjusted. During haze conditions, the operating hours can be extended by up to two hours.
“We will also refer the matter to local authorities, such as municipal councils and city halls, to encourage them to take similar measures,” he told reporters after visiting the family of three siblings who died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj here today.
The three siblings, aged eight to 18, were killed on Thursday after the motorcycle they were on collided with a lorry on Jalan Parit Haji Sirat in Kayu Ara Pason amid hazy weather and limited visibility.
Ahmad also advised road users to exercise greater caution and ensure safe visibility when driving in hazy conditions. — Bernama

Title: Air quality acceptable for now, Kedah schools to open as usual tomorrow
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 10 — All educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring areas in the state were recorded below 100 as of 2 pm today.
The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this was, however, subject to any further directives from the Ministry of Education and the relevant authorities.
“The Kedah JPN expresses its appreciation for the concern and decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, regarding the importance of safeguarding the safety, health and welfare of students and education personnel following the haze affecting several areas in the country.
“The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual,” the statement said.
The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.
“Schools should also pay close attention to students and education personnel experiencing health problems, particularly those who are sensitive to air quality conditions, and take appropriate action if any students or education personnel show signs of ill health.
“The Kedah JPN will continue to monitor developments in the haze situation and coordinate action with all District Education Offices and educational institutions based on the latest readings and directives from the authorities,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to prioritise mental health in World Mental Health Day post
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 —The public should prioritise their mental health and not hesitate to seek help when experiencing stress or feeling overburdened by the demands of daily life, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said mental health should be cared for alongside physical health, particularly when dealing with the demands of work, family and everyday life.
“In the midst of busy work, family and daily life, do not forget to look after our mental health just as we look after our physical health,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with World Mental Health Day today.
Fahmi said those who felt overwhelmed, exhausted or struggled to cope on their own should talk to someone they trusted and seek help if necessary.
He also reminded the public that taking a break and giving themselves some space was nothing to feel guilty about.
World Mental Health Day is observed on October 10 every year to raise public awareness of the importance of mental health worldwide. — Bernama

Title: President El-Sisi invites Malaysia’s King, PM to visit Egypt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt.
The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today.
“It speaks much to the depth and strength of the relations between our two countries,” he said at a joint press conference with Anwar at the Seri Perdana Complex, Putrajaya today. — Bernama

Title: Egypt president El-Sisi praises Malaysia for helping injured Gazans, backs Palestinian state
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has reaffirmed Egypt’s support for a two-state solution to the Palestinian issue, with an independent Palestinian state based on the July 4, 1967 borders and East Jerusalem as its capital.
He said the Palestinian issue remained central to West Asia and was among the key matters discussed during his meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“We stressed together (during the meeting) the necessity for a just and comprehensive settlement according to the international resolutions, and the two-state solution to ensure a Palestinian independent state is established,” he said at a joint press conference with Anwar in Putrajaya today.
El-Sisi also commended Malaysia’s support for the Palestinian people, particularly its humanitarian assistance and efforts to provide medical treatment for injured Palestinians from Gaza.
“I would be remiss if I didn't applaud Malaysia's supporting stance regarding the Palestinian issue and its keenness to provide humanitarian assistance to the Palestinian people and also hosting Palestinian second-injured people to get medical care here in Malaysia,” he said.
On the wider regional situation, El-Sisi said Egypt was making relentless efforts to halt the escalation in West Asia, stressing that collective efforts were necessary to establish peace and uphold international law.
“I would like to seize this opportunity to stress Egypt's relentless efforts to stop the escalation in West Asia,” he said, adding that all parties must work together to establish peace while respecting national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the principle of non-interference in domestic affairs.
“I just want to confirm here that there is a total convergence between myself and the prime minister regarding the issues of the region and the world, that the political and the diplomatic tracks, respecting international law, are the only way to find lasting and permanent solutions to the crisis in the Gulf,” he said.
He also said that both leaders discussed developments in the Horn of Africa and their potential implications for the wider region.
Malaysia and Egypt have maintained diplomatic relations since November 10, 1959, describing their partnership as founded on mutual respect, shared values, and common aspirations.
During El-Sisi’s state visit to Malaysia on October 9 and 10, the two countries elevated their bilateral relations to a Strategic Partnership and reaffirmed their commitment to closer cooperation across various sectors.
The two leaders also reaffirmed in a joint statement that Palestine remained the core issue in West Asia, rejecting plans to displace Palestinians and calling for the consolidation of the ceasefire in Gaza, unrestricted humanitarian assistance, and the implementation of relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions.
His state visit to Malaysia — his first to the country since assuming office in June 2014 — is at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. El-Sisi is accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior Egyptian government officials. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia and Egypt eye easier travel, more business as trade surges, says PM
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Malaysia and Egypt will focus on expanding trade and investment cooperation, improving flight connectivity and exploring new areas of economic collaboration at a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting, agreed upon by the two countries’ foreign ministers, would provide a platform to translate growing bilateral ties into broader economic opportunities.
He said bilateral trade had increased 74.7 per cent this year, but stressed that the growth came from a low base, leaving considerable room for further expansion.
“We have achieved this phenomenal increase this year, rising to 74.7 per cent of trade, but then it is from a very, very low base,” said the prime minister.
Anwar was speaking at a joint press conference with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in conjunction with the latter’s two-day state visit to Malaysia.
He said Malaysia saw considerable potential to expand cooperation with Egypt in several sectors, including semiconductors, electrical and electronics (E&E), agriculture and pharmaceuticals.
Malaysia was also looking at emerging economies, including Brics countries, as potential sources of pharmaceutical products, with Egypt among the countries that could meet its needs.
“Egypt has the potential to become a destination for sourcing pharmaceuticals,” said Anwar.
He said improved air connectivity, including more regular flights, would also be important in facilitating trade, investment and tourism between the two countries.
Anwar described Egypt as an important country in the Arab world and Africa, adding that closer engagement would give Malaysia greater opportunities to expand its economic presence in the region.
Earlier, the prime minister and his counterpart held a four-eyed meeting at the Seri Perdana Complex here today, marking a significant step towards elevating Malaysia-Egypt relations to a strategic partnership after more than six decades of diplomatic ties.
The meeting, held in conjunction with El-Sisi’s two-day state visit to Malaysia, provided an opportunity for both leaders to review bilateral cooperation, explore new areas of collaboration and exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest.
The Egyptian president, who is undertaking his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014, arrived at the complex at 12.58pm for a series of official engagements aimed at strengthening political, economic and diplomatic relations between the two nations.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh-largest trading partner in Africa, with total bilateral trade valued at RM3.08 billion (US$0.72 billion).
Malaysia’s exports to Egypt amounted to RM2.55 billion (US$0.60 billion), while imports totalled RM530 million (US$0.12 billion).
From January to August 2026, bilateral trade surged 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$0.87 billion). — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry drafting national registry for persons with disabilities to improve service planning
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through its Family Health Development Division’s Persons with Disabilities (PWD) Sector, has initiated strategic discussions on the development of the MOH PWD Strategic Plan.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was also drafting a proposal for a national-level PWD Registry (OKU Registry), which would incorporate data and needs profiles of the cerebral palsy (CP) community.
“This step shows that your voices are being heard and translated into structured action at the ministry level to plan a service delivery system driven by actual data.
“Approaches such as the CP Living Library featured in this symposium are highly significant. Clinical knowledge provides medical and scientific evidence, while your lived experiences offer a human and empathetic perspective,” he said.
He was speaking at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Cerebral Palsy Symposium, organised by Gabungan Anak-Anak Palsi Serebrum (GAPS) at the Shah Alam Convention Centre here today.
MOH records showed that 1,076 children with CP had been registered and received early intervention services at health clinics nationwide from 2016 to 2025.
Speaking to reporters, Dzulkefly said the strategic plan was still at an early stage, but it was important to ensure that the needs of individuals with CP continued to receive attention throughout their lives.
He said CP required not only care during childhood but also continuous support as individuals transitioned into adolescence and adulthood.
“This is a lifelong need. We want to ensure this group has the opportunity to lead lives like everyone else, including in terms of careers, social relationships and starting a family.
“Our challenge is to ensure they are not excluded from the support system after leaving school. They need more than empathy and sympathy; they need an ecosystem that enables them to live a normal, dignified and inclusive life throughout their lives,” he said.
On the expected timeline for developing the PWD Registry, Dzulkefly said the initiative would be implemented continuously through an approach of ongoing improvement.
He said data collection had to begin in an organised and structured manner to ensure the registry contained high-quality data that could support more effective service planning. — Bernama

Title: Eight-metre-deep sinkhole forces closure of Gua Musang-Kota Bharu road
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 10 — The Federal Route FT08 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu Road, near Taman Rekreasi Kesedar here, has been closed to all vehicles today due to a sinkhole measuring about eight metres deep.
The incident, reported at 9.05am, affected a stretch of about nine metres between Sections 205.556 and 205.564, involving the alignment of Packages 3B and 3C of the Central Spine Road (LTU) project.
According to reports by the Gua Musang Public Works Department (JKR) and Roadcare (M) Sdn Bhd, the closure wasn implemented to ensure the safety of road users while further action is taken.
Road users are advised to use alternative routes via FT2747, namely Jalan Pulai to Bandar Baharu Gua Musang.
Meanwhile, Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo, when contacted, confirmed the incident and advised road users to comply with instructions from the authorities. — Bernama

Title: Wider electricity bill protection, RM15b National Grid investment will benefit households, says TNB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) has welcomed the RM15 billion investment to strengthen the National Grid under Budget 2027, alongside measures to protect domestic electricity consumers and improve energy security.
In a statement today, TNB said the investment forms part of its RM43 billion programme from 2025 to 2027 to modernise the country’s electricity infrastructure and meet growing demand.
“We will continue to work closely with the government and stakeholders to ensure that the development of the nation’s energy system benefits the people, supports economic growth and contributes to a more sustainable future for generations to come,” TNB president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Shamsul Ahmad said.
The utility company also backed the government’s decision to extend electricity bill protection to households consuming up to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) monthly, compared with 600 kWh previously, until December 31.
The measure is expected to benefit more than eight million households, representing up to 90 per cent of domestic electricity consumers.
TNB said it would also work more closely with the government to accelerate rural electrification projects, including improvements to electricity supply in Orang Asli settlements, tahfiz and pondok schools.
It also reaffirmed its commitment to expanding renewable energy capacity and supporting the country’s target of achieving a 70 per cent share of renewable energy in installed electricity generation capacity by 2050.

Title: Khazanah backs Budget 2027, pledges support for semiconductor growth and energy transition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Khazanah Nasional Berhad today welcomed the Malaysia Madani Budget 2027, describing it as a people-centric blueprint that strengthens the country’s long-term competitiveness while addressing immediate concerns over the cost of living and wages.
In a statement following the tabling of the budget by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Khazanah managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir said the spending plan arrived at a critical juncture as Malaysia navigates geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions and elevated fuel prices linked to the ongoing conflict in West Asia.
He said Budget 2027, themed
“Malaysia MADANI: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”
, balances economic growth with inclusivity by focusing on strategic sectors such as semiconductors, energy transition, infrastructure, enterprise development and talent development.
According to Amirul Feisal, these priorities are essential for strengthening Malaysia’s industrial base, increasing economic complexity and creating higher-value opportunities for businesses and workers.
“Importantly, the Budget places emphasis not only on growth, but on quality growth,” he said.
Khazanah also welcomed measures aimed at ensuring broader participation in national development, including initiatives benefiting workers, youth, entrepreneurs, Bumiputera companies, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and communities facing economic and climate-related challenges.
The sovereign wealth fund said it fully supports the government’s move to raise the living wage benchmark for employees of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) to RM3,400 per month, in line with efforts to increase labour’s share of gross domestic product (GDP).
On heritage conservation, Amirul Feisal said Khazanah would continue restoration work under its Dana Warisan investments through the broader Warisan KL initiative, including ongoing projects at the Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad Complex and Carcosa.
Khazanah also announced a collaboration with the Penang and Selangor state governments to strengthen Malaysia’s semiconductor and advanced manufacturing ecosystem.
Under the initiative, Penang, Selangor and Khazanah will each contribute RM50 million to a Strategic Investment Fund, bringing the fund’s initial size to RM150 million.
The fund is aimed at supporting the growth of high-potential Malaysian companies, while complementing Budget 2027’s emphasis on vendor development, innovation and market expansion.
In support of Bumiputera business growth, Khazanah said Dana Ciptawan will be expanded to RM250 million in collaboration with Teraju to assist Bumiputera and Malaysian mid-tier companies.
The fund also welcomed government ambitions in energy transition and climate resilience, citing Tenaga Nasional Berhad’s investment in the national electricity grid and UEM Lestra’s RM1 billion renewable energy investment as key enablers of Malaysia’s energy security, affordability and sustainability agenda.
Amirul Feisal said Khazanah remains committed to supporting national development through initiatives such as Dana Impak, Jelawang Capital, Dana Ciptawan, Dana Warisan, K-Youth, Bakat Madani and Yayasan Hasanah.
He said the organisation would continue working with other GLICs under the Ministry of Finance’s GEAR-uP programme to mobilise capital through disciplined investments, catalytic partnerships and impact-driven programmes that contribute to Malaysia’s long-term competitiveness.

Title: Egypt president El-Sisi accorded state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara on Saturday on the occasion of his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014, at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Sultan Ibrahim graciously welcomed the arrival of El-Sisi at 10.08 am.
Also in attendance were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Following the welcoming ceremony, El-Sisi inspected a guard of honour comprising 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment.
The welcoming ceremony at the Istana Negara parade square began with a rendition of the national anthems of both countries by the Royal Ranger Regiment band led by Captain (DOM) Mohd Fahmy Harun, followed by a 21-gun salute by the 41st Battery of the Royal Artillery Regiment.
The Egyptian president then inspected a guard of honour comprising five officers and 89 personnel from the three branches of the Malaysian Armed Forces, namely the Malaysian Army, the Royal Malaysian Navy, and the Royal Malaysian Air Force, led by Major Muhammad Waqiyudin Abd Rahman.
His Majesty then grants an audience to El-Sisi and the Egyptian delegation and witnessed a presentation of royal tokens of appreciation ceremony at Dewan Seri Maharaja.
Sultan Ibrahim then hosted a state banquet at the Grand Banquet Hall in honour of El-Sisi and the Egyptian government delegation.
El-Sisi’s visit is the first by an Egyptian president to Malaysia for nearly three decades. The last visit, by former President Mohamed Hosni Mubarak, took place in November 1997 when he attended the G-15 Summit in Kuala Lumpur. Mubarak also undertook an official visit as the Egyptian Vice President in 1979.
Wisma Putra in a statement on Friday said El-Sisi, who is accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior Egyptian government officials, is also scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting Anwar Ibrahim to take stock of progress in bilateral cooperation and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
Both leaders will then witness the exchange of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) between Malaysia and Egypt, followed by an official hi-tea at Seri Perdana Complex hosted by the prime minister at Seri Perdana Complex.
Malaysia and Egypt have established diplomatic relations since 1959.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh largest trading partner in Africa.
Malaysia’s total trade with Egypt was valued at RM3.08 billion (US$720 million), with exports valued at RM2.55 billion (US$600 million) and imports at RM530 million (US$120 million).
From January to August 2026, total trade between the two countries increased by 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$870 million). — Bernama

Title: Man loses over RM12m in suspected crypto theft
Article:
IPOH, Oct 10 — A man lost about RM12.47 million after his crypto assets were believed to have been stolen through unauthorised access to his digital wallet.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 38-year-old victim realised this at about 1 pm yesterday while he was in the Teluk Intan area.
He said the victim realised that a sum of his crypto assets had been transferred out of his digital wallet without his knowledge or consent.
“Preliminary investigation found that the transaction involved the transfer of crypto assets through a blockchain network.
“Police are conducting further investigations to identify those involved and tracking the flow of transactions with assistance from the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department’s (CCID) Crypto Unit,” he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Mohd Alwi advised the public to be careful about phishing and online scams, avoid clicking on suspicious links, always monitor their digital wallet transactions, act immediately if they suspect their accounts have been hacked and strengthen their digital security measures. — Bernama

Title: Brace for bad weather: Thunderstorms expected in all Malaysian states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 —The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning, with heavy rain and strong winds expected in Perlis, Kuala Lumpur and 12 other states until 6 pm today.
MetMalaysia, in a statement, said that the adverse weather was expected to affect several areas in Kedah, namely Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik and Baling, as well as Timur Laut and Barat Daya in Penang.
In Perak, the affected areas are Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak and Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai and Jeli, as well as the whole of Terengganu.
The same warning has also been issued for Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang, and Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Petaling and Hulu Langat in Selangor.
In addition, adverse weather is expected across Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, as well as Kulai and Johor Bahru in Johor.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Lubok Antu in Sri Aman Division. In Sabah, the affected areas are Tawau, Semporna, Kunak and Lahad Datu; Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Sandakan, Telupid, Labuk, Sugut, and Paitan); West Coast (Kota Belud and Ranau) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: Malaysia awaits Indonesia’s response on haze operation as talks continue, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Malaysia is still awaiting a response through official diplomatic channels on arrangements for its offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
Fahmi, who is also the government spokesperson, said discussions had taken place directly between the countries’ leaders and expressed hope that their good relations would allow follow-up action.
“I believe that the matter has been conveyed, that discussions have taken place directly with the Indonesian president, and we believe that the good relations today will make it possible for follow-up action to be taken.
“However, so far (as of this morning) no response has been conveyed through Wisma Putra.
“We will wait a little longer,” Fahmi told a press conference after officiating the World Post Day at the Pos Malaysia headquarters here today.
Fahmi was responding to reporters who asked for an update of efforts taken to improve air quality in Malaysia.
He added that current and immediate measures such as temporary shutting schools and postponing school Sports Day were among other actions taken.
“Similarly for other sectors, keep a lookout on updates from respective ministries on next course of action, he said.
Indonesia had earlier agreed to Malaysia’s offer of assistance during Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s meeting with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in September.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said on October 7 that the two countries were still negotiating operational arrangements, including how the mission would be carried out and where the Malaysian team would be deployed.
Malaysia’s proposed assistance includes a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and Royal Malaysian Air Force.

Title: King confers Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara to El-Sisi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim today consented to the conferring of the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) award to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, who is currently in Malaysia on a two-day state visit.
El-Sisi was conferred the award at Istana Negara in a special ceremony at Dewan Seri Maharaja prior to a state banquet hosted in honour of the Egyptian leader, who arrived in the country yesterday.
Also at the ceremony were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, dignitaries, and an Egyptian delegation.
Earlier, El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony the Istana Negara parade square upon his arrival at 10.08 am.
El-Sisi’s visit, at the invitation of Sultan Ibrahim, is the first by an Egyptian president to Malaysia for nearly three decades. The last visit, by former President Mohamed Hosni Mubarak, took place in November 1997 when he attended the G-15 Summit in Kuala Lumpur. Mubarak also undertook an official visit as the Egyptian Vice President in 1979.
Malaysia and Egypt have established diplomatic relations since 1959. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: HKL plans facility upgrades and digital health system rollout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The government’s increased allocation for healthcare under Budget 2027 is seen as a catalyst for Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) to upgrade its infrastructure and accelerate its transition to a fully digital hospital.
HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K R Nair said the allocation would help the 156-year-old hospital modernise its electrical systems and other facilities, as well as strengthen its information technology infrastructure.
“We are quite happy because Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has increased the healthcare allocation by RM1.2 billion compared with last year. This will help us improve facilities for patients. HKL is already 156 years old, so our electrical systems and other infrastructure are different.
“We are already replacing our lifts and upgrading other facilities, and the additional budget will help us upgrade most of the systems as we are planning to go as a full total Health Information System hospital, that means completely computerised,” he told Bernama when met at the Community Programme and Healthy Lifestyle Fun Run held in conjunction with World Heart Day 2026 at Perdana Botanical Gardens here today.
He said HKL was among 16 hospitals scheduled to implement the Health Information System next year, with RM200 million allocated for the initiative.
He said the system would enable specialists from different disciplines to access patients’ medical information electronically, streamlining hospital operations, and reducing the need for patients to repeatedly provide the same information during consultations.
“This will make things easier and improve staff management. Patients will also benefit because they will not have to answer the same questions at every stage of their treatment, as their information will be accessible to specialists across different disciplines,” he said.
On efforts to address non-communicable diseases (NCDs), Dr Harikrishna said the funding was crucial as it would also enable HKL to procure newer medicines and carry out more medical procedures, thereby improving access to treatment.
“With sufficient funding, we can procure more of these medicines and carry out more procedures. We also outsource some simpler cases under Skim Perubatan MADANI, managed by ProtectHealth, and the allocation for this has also been increased,” he said.
Increased funding for outsourcing services would help reduce waiting times, enabling patients to receive treatment sooner and lower the risk of complications.
“Expanding outsourcing services will help reduce waiting times, lower the risk of complications and improve patients’ access to medicines and other treatments. This will be beneficial not only for HKL but also for the Ministry of Health (MOH) as a whole,” he also said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, announced RM47.7 billion for the MOH when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, up from RM46.5 billion last year.
He also announced RM1.2 billion for the maintenance and repair of public hospitals and clinics, including upgrading the remaining dilapidated clinics, while the allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals was increased to RM200 million, alongside expanded collaboration enabling the public healthcare sector to use private healthcare facilities. — Bernama

Title: Govt triples Postal Service Fund to RM150m, eyes  Q1 2027 rollout to support rural deliveries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The government has allocated RM150 million to activate the Postal Service Fund, which is now expected to begin operating in the first quarter of 2027, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the initial fund will, among other things, support the Universal Service Obligation (USO), particularly the delivery of letters to rural areas, remote locations and islands.
“The government has agreed to activate the Postal Fund, which will hopefully begin operating in the first quarter of 2027, with initial funding of RM150 million,” Fahmi told a press conference after officiating the World Post Day celebration at the Pos Malaysia headquarters here today.
Fahmi had previously said in January that the government was targeting the fund’s introduction by the third quarter of 2026.
The RM150 million allocation is three times the RM50 million funding previously announced for the programme.
Acknowledging the changing landscape of e-commerce and digital technology, Fahmi said this also meant that adjustments might be needed to policies, legislation and operational practices governing the postal sector.
He stressed that the welfare of postal and courier workers must also be protected, including ensuring fair compensation and decent wages.
“We do not want a situation where there is excessive imbalance,” he said.
He added that MCMC had begun engagement with e-commerce service providers, with discussions to be extended to major courier companies.
The commission would also continue discussions with regulatory agencies, including the Royal Malaysia Police and the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency, to address complaints involving e-commerce transactions and parcel deliveries.
Fahmi said the Postal Service Fund had been provided for under legislation since 2012, but previous governments had not taken steps to operationalise it.
He said he had also asked that the fund’s scope not be limited to conventional postal services, noting that deliveries of goods to remote communities could also serve an important function.
“MCMC will make a full announcement in due course to explain the functions of the Postal Fund,” he added.
The Postal Service Fund was provided for under Section 98 of the Postal Services Act 2012, which places it under MCMC’s control and operation.
Section 98 also explained how the fund is to comprise money provided by Parliament and contributions from licensees or other parties.
Under this provision, it also permits spending on universal postal services, expanding and improving the postal network, technology and other postal-related purposes determined by the minister.
In-line with the World Post Day, Fahmi said the Communications Ministry, MCMC and Pos Malaysia would work together on special initiatives to mark the 70th anniversary of National Postal Day, including efforts to strengthen ties between Pos Malaysia and the Malaysian Philatelic Society.

Title: Abang Johari appreciates RM16.2b allocation for Sarawak in Budget 2027
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 10 — Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg expressed his appreciation to the Madani Government, led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, for the increase in the federal allocation for Sarawak to RM16.2 billion under Budget 2027.
“I extend my gratitude to the federal Government for increasing the annual allocation for Sarawak to RM16.2 billion,” he said while speaking at the parade and grand assembly held in conjunction with the 80th birthday celebration of the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, at Padang Merdeka here today.
Yesterday, during the Budget 2027 presentation, Anwar announced allocations of RM18.7 billion for Sabah and RM16.2 billion for Sarawak for 2027; in comparison, under the Budget 2026, Sabah received RM17.6 billion while Sarawak obtained RM15.1 billion.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari noted that throughout his career in security, politics, and administration including as a member of the Federal Cabinet, Tun Wan Junaidi has witnessed various pivotal events that shaped the history of both the nation and Sarawak.
He said Tun Wan Junaidi’s extensive experience in security, law, constitutional matters, and administration provided a comprehensive perspective on the dynamics of governance, as well as the challenges and responsibilities involved in ensuring the stability and progress of the state and the country.
A total of 107 contingents across seven categories comprising government agencies, statutory bodies, the private sector, educational institutions, and non-governmental organisations (NGOs), involving about 5,000 participants took part in the parade.
In addition, the official birthday celebrations for the Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Sarawak are taking place from October 8 until tomorrow, featuring various events such as a thanksgiving ceremony and an interfaith thanksgiving ceremony, the Sarawak State Awards Investiture Ceremony, a state banquet, and a tea reception. — Bernama

Title: Haze sees Malaysian respiratory infections rise 10.43pc, conjunctivitis 26.47pc
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Cases of upper respiratory tract infections rose 10.43 per cent, while conjunctivitis cases increased 26.47 per cent, according to haze-related disease monitoring at 78 selected Health Ministry (MOH) facilities nationwide.
In a statement today, the ministry said upper respiratory tract infection cases increased from 3,509 in Epidemiological Week (EW) 39 to 3,875 in EW40, while conjunctivitis cases rose from 102 to 129 over the same period.
However, asthma cases fell 13.64 per cent, from 535 to 462.
The ministry said it would continue to strengthen surveillance of haze-related illnesses as exposure to polluted air could affect health, particularly among children, the elderly, pregnant women and people with lung or heart conditions.
As of 8 am today, 32 air quality monitoring stations across eight states and two Federal Territories recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the Unhealthy range of 101 to 200.
The MOH advised the public, particularly those in areas with unhealthy API readings, to take precautions, including avoiding or postponing outdoor activities. Children, the elderly and people with lung or heart conditions should take extra care.
Those who need to be outdoors during hazy conditions were advised to wear suitable face masks, such as N95 masks. Motorists should also slow down or stop at a safe location if visibility is limited.
The ministry urged the public to check API readings regularly through official Department of Environment (DOE) channels and take appropriate precautions based on local air quality.
It also reminded the public to remain vigilant, minimise exposure to haze and prioritise their health and that of their families. — Bernama

Title: API reaches unhealthy levels in 33 areas across Malaysia by 10am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — A total of 33 areas recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 10 am today, with Batu Pahat, Johor, recording the highest reading at 190.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas in Johor recording unhealthy API levels were Tangkak (186), Larkin (185), Pasir Gudang (184), Segamat (181), Kluang (177), Kota Tinggi (172), and Pengerang (169).
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas were Seremban (183), Nilai (179), and Port Dickson (164), while in Melaka, three areas were affected: Bukit Rambai (175), Melaka City (173), and Alor Gajah (173).
Six areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy API readings: Shah Alam (167), Johan Setia (165), Petaling Jaya (161), Klang (157), Banting (154), and Kuala Selangor (152); meanwhile, in Perak, the areas were Tasek Ipoh (174), Pegoh Ipoh (170), Tanjung Malim (168), and Seri Manjung (152).
Batu Muda and Cheras in the capital recorded readings of 169 and 175 respectively, while Putrajaya recorded 167.
Other affected areas include Rompin (168), Temerloh (139), and Indera Mahkota Kuantan (141) in Pahang; Seberang Perai (123) in Penang; as well as Kuching (153) and Samarahan (109) in Sarawak.
Meanwhile, 35 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at the moderate level.
API readings between 0 and 50 indicate good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; while readings exceeding 300 are considered hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Paying a carer for your parents or grandparents? Budget 2027 proposes tax relief even for non-medical care
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — For Malaysian taxpayers paying a carer or for care services for their parents or grandparents, the government is proposing to allow them to claim tax relief even if the care is not for medical reasons.
Currently, Malaysians can claim a maximum RM8,000 tax relief for spending on these services in Malaysia for their parents and grandparents, who are required to be living in Malaysia:
Medical treatment at clinics and hospitals
Maximum RM1,000: Full medical examination and vaccinations
Dental treatment (excluding cosmetic dental treatment)
Treatment and care at home, day care centres and residential care centres
Based on existing Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) rules, claims must be supported by the relevant documents, including receipts and medical certification where required:
A medical practitioner registered with the Malaysian Dental Council must certify that their medical condition needs dental treatment;
A medical practitioner registered with the Malaysian Medical Council must certify that their medical condition needs medical treatment, medical examination or care services.
This means that taxpayers currently can only claim for their parents’ or grandparents’ care services if it involves medical care.
Yesterday, in Budget 2027, the Finance Ministry proposed that Malaysians be allowed to claim tax relief on “all types of care expenses” for their parents and grandparents at home, day care centres and residential care centres, instead of limiting it to “medical care”.
Under this proposed change starting from the year of assessment 2027, you will still need a carer’s written declaration or a copy of the carer’s work permit together with receipts, but you can make the tax relief claim without “requiring any verification from a registered medical practitioner”.
Good news for older persons needing care services
In Budget 2027, the Malaysian government also proposes to reduce the current service tax of eight per cent to six per cent for care centre services for older persons, starting from January 2027.
It also proposes to exempt care centre services from service tax if the annual fees for each older person do not exceed RM96,000.
In other words, if an older person is paying RM8,000 or less every month for care centre services, there will be no service tax.
But if the care centre charges more than RM8,000 every month for an older person’s care services, the six per cent service tax could apply, depending on how the exemption is implemented.
Just as an example, if an older person is paying RM8,100 every month for such care services, a six per cent tax on the full fee would mean an additional RM486 per month or RM5,832 per year.
On July 16, 2026, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong had in a Dewan Rakyat Special Chamber session noted that the government was carrying out studies to identify categories for care centres for older persons that offer basic or premium care services, in order to determine a targeted service tax collection.
He had said the Finance Ministry would ensure vulnerable groups are not affected by service tax on care services for older persons.

Title: Lorry driver tests positive for drugs after ploughing into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam, claims brake failure
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 10 — The driver of a lorry that crashed into 11 other vehicles at a traffic light junction in Alam Budiman yesterday has tested positive for drugs, police said today.
According to Bernama, Shah Alam police chief ACP Sarudin Samah said a urine screening test conducted on the 51-year-old driver found traces of amphetamine and methamphetamine.
He said the driver was detained to assist investigations under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and was expected to be remanded at the Shah Alam Court today.
Preliminary investigations found that the driver claimed to have experienced brake problems while travelling downhill from Puncak Perdana towards Puncak Alam at about 4.20pm.
Sarudin said the lorry subsequently veered into the opposite lane and crashed into 11 vehicles waiting at the traffic lights at the Alam Budiman three-way junction along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari.
A 58-year-old man driving a Subaru XV sport utility vehicle suffered serious head injuries and was receiving treatment in the red zone of UiTM Hospital Puncak Alam.
His 53-year-old wife and their 17-year-old grandson, who were travelling in the same vehicle, were also hospitalised and reported to be in stable condition.
Another motorist, a 29-year-old man driving a Perodua Myvi, sustained bodily injuries but was reported to be in stable condition.
Footage of the crash, showing a lorry travelling against the flow of traffic before colliding with several vehicles at the junction, went viral on social media yesterday.
Police urged anyone with information about the incident to contact investigating officer Inspector Abdul Nasser Peping at 012-286 3875. — Bernama
